To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Phe-TyrMet-Glu, the amino acid sequence of the first complementarity- determining region of the heavy chain of PC-binding proteins, inhibits PC binding to McPC603 and to HOPC8; (2) other structurally related synthetic peptides inhibit PC binding to McPc603 and to HOpC8 non-specifically; and (3) the surface-simulation peptides, which were constructed to mimic the binding site of McPC6o3,
(i) Phe-Tyr- Met-Glu is not unique to the binding site and (ii) the surface-simulation peptides do not duplicate the combining sites of PC binding proteins.

(1) the amino-acid sequence of Phe-Ty-Met-Glu, which occurs in the first CDR of the immunoglobulins heavy chain in 89% anti-PC myloma proteins is not involved in binding of PC, and (2) the surface-simulation peptides, which were constructed to mimic the binding site of McPC 603, are ineffective in inhibiting PC binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inhibition of the binding of PC by synthetic peptides, but we do not find any evidence to support the idea that the Phe-Tyr- Met-Glu sequence is specifically involved in PC binding.
the design of peptides to inhibit the binding of phosphorylcholines to antibodies.
the inhibition of the binding of PC and its derivatives to PC-binding antibodies using synthetic peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all peptides tested in this work inhibit PC binding to PC-binding proteins by non-specific mechanisms.
all these peptides are not specific to the PC binding site and are not effective in inhibiting the reaction.
none of the peptides tested in this work is capable of inhibiting PC binding to McPC603 and that none of them can simulate the combining site of the antibody.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
all these peptides are poor PC mimics and that Phe-Tyr- Met-Glu is a better PC mimic than any other tetrapeptide we have tested.
the Phe-Tyr- Met-Glu peptide is the most effective inhibitor of PC binding to PC-binding antibodies.
the amino-acid sequence of the combining site of an antibody is not a sufficient description for its specificity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tetrapeptide Phe-Tyr- Met-Glu is not involved in PC binding.
the amino-acid sequence Tyr-Met-Glu does not seem to be involved in the binding of PC.
it is difficult to inhibit the binding of an epitope to a protein using peptides.
